headline.text: Indo SMC: a freshly-listed FRP junction-box maker growing revenue 249% over 3 years, with real ROE to match.

subhead.text: Revenue went from ₹7.29 Cr (FY23) to ₹310 Cr (FY26) with a 34.1% ROE — and a first confirmed export shipment to Oman landed just this year.

p1_engine.eyebrow: Explosive, real growth — now with public-market capital to fund the next phase

blocks.text: This is a genuinely explosive, independently-confirmed growth trajectory: revenue grew from ₹7.29 Cr (FY23) to ₹28.03 Cr (FY24) to ₹138.78 Cr (FY25, +395% YoY) to ₹310 Cr (FY26) — a 3-year sales CAGR of 249% per screener.in. PAT grew 414% YoY in FY25 to ₹15.44 Cr, reaching ₹32 Cr by FY26. ROE stands at 34.1% (1-yr) and 43% (3-yr average), with ROCE at 33.9% — among the strongest return profiles of any company profiled in this project.

It designs and manufactures products for electrical, industrial, and infrastructure applications — FRP gratings, manhole covers, junction boxes, and electricity meter boxes — meeting BIS standards IS:13410 and IS:14772 for SMC junction boxes, with a real, independently-found certification stack (ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015) that the HVT sheet itself left blank on the moat pillar.

It completed a BSE SME IPO — listing 21 Jan 2026 at ₹149 (flat vs. issue price), raising ~₹92 Cr via a fresh issue of 61.71 lakh shares — meaning the HVT sheet's 'unlisted-public' ownership tag is now outdated and should be corrected to 'listed.' It operates four manufacturing facilities across Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan across three business divisions: SMC (energy meter enclosures), FRP (gratings and allied products), and Electrical Components (CTs/PTs, feeder pillars, switchgears).

**The HVT sheet's own gap research (Oman/Gulf exports with US/Germany samples) is now confirmed and updated**: the company achieved its first actual FRP export shipment to Oman in Q1 FY27, and newly installed pultrusion machines at its Ahmedabad plant now enable structural composite products including pultruded spar caps. Q1 FY27 revenue grew 135.96% YoY to ₹88.12 Cr, and the order book grew from ₹144.58 Cr (Jul 2025) to ₹283.19 Cr (Nov 2025), including a ~₹66.6 Cr order from Indian Railways. Independent confirmation of ASTM certification status for full US/Germany market entry was not found this session.

insights.point: A real, growing SMC/FRP market with **direct policy-linked demand from India's grid and infrastructure spend**.
insights.evidence: Global SMC market: $1.1B (2024) to $1.8B by 2033 (6.2%/yr), with India's EV and renewable-energy sectors reportedly boosting SMC usage by 24%; BIS standards IS:13410/IS:14772 set the domestic compliance bar Indo SMC's products already meet.

insights.point: **Sintex is the established brand incumbent**, but no disclosed financials were found to benchmark Indo SMC's exceptional growth rate against.
insights.evidence: Sintex is named as a major established SMC junction-box/electrical-enclosure brand in India, but revenue/margin figures were not independently found — meaning Indo SMC's 249% 3-year sales CAGR can't be directly compared to the incumbent's growth rate.

insights.point: **Government tender demand (Indian Railways) is a real, large, and growing order-book component**, not just private-sector growth.
insights.evidence: The ~₹66.6 Cr Indian Railways order and the order book's growth from ₹144.58 Cr to ₹283.19 Cr in just four months (Jul-Nov 2025) both point to genuine institutional demand momentum, independent of the company's own IPO narrative.

reflect.text: One of the strongest growth-and-returns profiles in this entire project — a genuinely explosive, independently-confirmed 3-year revenue trajectory backed by real ROE/ROCE, a growing government-linked order book, and a fresh public listing to fund further capacity. The main open question is durability: whether 249% 3-year CAGR growth is sustainable or reflects a low, early-stage base that naturally decelerates.

items.title: Converting the Oman export beachhead into broader US/Germany market entry via ASTM certification
items.body: The HVT sheet's own gap research named this directly, and this session confirms real progress: the first Oman FRP export shipment landed in Q1 FY27. Pursuing ASTM certification to unlock the larger US/Germany markets (where only samples have been sent so far) is the credible next step, building on demonstrated export execution rather than starting from zero.
items.source: HVT gap research (whalesbook.com Q1 FY27 update).

guesslabel.text: Possibilities, not prescriptions — and the honest first step here is stress-testing whether the 249% growth rate is durable.

items.title: Assess whether the exceptional growth rate reflects a durable demand curve or a low early-stage base
items.body: A 3-year sales CAGR of 249% is exceptional by any standard — confirming what share of that growth came from a genuinely expanding addressable market (grid infrastructure, EV, government tenders) versus simply scaling off a very small FY23 base would clarify how much of this growth rate to expect going forward.

takeaway.text: One of the strongest growth-and-returns stories in this entire project — a real 249% 3-year sales CAGR, 34.1% ROE, and a fresh IPO to fund the next phase, now backed by a confirmed first export shipment to Oman. **Whether this growth rate is durable as the base scales up is the one open question.**
